question: The Vakataka dynasty was directly related to which Gupta emperor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra Gupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vakataka dynasty ruled in central and southern India from the 3rd to 5th century CE.**
 
• **The Gupta dynasty** was a powerful and influential dynasty that ruled in northern India from the **4th to 6th century CE.**
 
• ** The Vakataka dynasty** was directly related to Chandra Gupta II, who was** a Gupta emperor.**
 
• **Chandra Gupta, I was the founder of the Gupta dynasty** and ruled from 320 to 335 CE, which was before the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• Shree Gupta, the grandfather of Chandra Gupta I, laid the foundation of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Samudra Gupta was a Gupta emperor who ruled from 335 to 375 CE, which was also before the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• **Option 4, Chandra Gupta II, is the correct answer as he was the Gupta emperor who was directly related to the Vakataka dynasty.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Gupta Empire :

 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from the early 4th century CE to the late 6th century CE.
 
• At its zenith, from approximately 319 to 467 CE, it covered much of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This period is considered the Golden Age of India by historians.
 
• The ruling dynasty of the empire was founded by the king Sri Gupta; the most notable rulers of the dynasty were Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II alias Vikramaditya.
